title: Lost in Chunks
description: chunk(items, size) splits a list into consecutive pieces of length size. The last piece may be shorter.
code:
def chunk(items, size):
    return [items[i:i + size] for i in range(0, len(items) - size, size)]
solution:
def chunk(items, size):
    return [items[i:i + size] for i in range(0, len(items), size)]
hint: List the start indexes the range produces for 6 items and size 2.
explanation: `range(0, len(items) - size, size)` stops one chunk too early, so the last chunk is dropped. Slicing past the end of a list is safe in Python, so `range(0, len(items), size)` handles a short final chunk on its own.
